stem.text: A vertical shaft is drilled to an unknown depth D meters, where \( D > 4 \). The amount of dissolved salt per meter of depth is \( f(h) = 2 \sin{\left(\frac{h^{2}}{4} \right)} + 9 \) grams per meter for \( 0 \le h \le 4 \), where h is the depth in meters. Below depth 4 the amount per meter is an unknown continuous function g(h), and \( 0 \le g(h) \le b(h) \) for \( h \ge 4 \), where b is a function with \( \int_{4}^{\infty} b(h)\,dh = 10 \). Let T be the total amount of dissolved salt, in grams, along the whole shaft. Write an expression involving integrals for T, and explain why \( T \le 50 \). Use a calculator for any numerical work.

answer_key.label: \( T = \int_{0}^{4} f(h)\,dh + \int_{4}^{D} g(h)\,dh \), and \( T \le 50 \) because \( \int_{0}^{4} f(h)\,dh \approx 39.219 \) and \( \int_{4}^{D} g(h)\,dh \le \int_{4}^{\infty} b(h)\,dh = 10 \).

worked_solution.text: The model changes at depth 4, so split the total there: \( T = \int_{0}^{4} f(h)\,dh + \int_{4}^{D} g(h)\,dh \).
Since \( 0 \le g(h) \le b(h) \) and the interval from 4 to D lies inside the interval from 4 to infinity, \( \int_{4}^{D} g(h)\,dh \le 10 \). So \( T \le 39.219 + 10 < 50 \).

options.label: \( T = \int_{0}^{4} f(h)\,dh + \int_{4}^{D} g(h)\,dh + C \), and \( T \le 50 \) because \( \int_{0}^{4} f(h)\,dh \approx 39.219 \) and \( \int_{4}^{D} g(h)\,dh \le \int_{4}^{\infty} b(h)\,dh = 10 \).
options.derivation: a constant of integration attached to a sum of definite integrals

options.label: \( T = \int_{0}^{4} f(h)\,dh + g(D) - g(4) \), and \( T \le 50 \) because \( \int_{0}^{4} f(h)\,dh \approx 39.219 \) and \( \int_{4}^{D} g(h)\,dh \le \int_{4}^{\infty} b(h)\,dh = 10 \).
options.derivation: the integral of g from the split depth to D written as g(D) - g(split), as though g were its own antiderivative

options.label: \( T = \int_{0}^{4} f(h)\,dh + g(h), \text{ where } g(h) = \int_{4}^{D} g(h)\,dh \), and \( T \le 50 \) because \( \int_{0}^{4} f(h)\,dh \approx 39.219 \) and \( \int_{4}^{D} g(h)\,dh \le \int_{4}^{\infty} b(h)\,dh = 10 \).
options.derivation: the unknown function set equal to its own integral and substituted for the second piece
